newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sterling Eurobond seen next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sterling Eurobond seen next week.

text.p: Brazil expects to launch its upcoming 150-200 million 10-year sterling Eurobond next week, and not this week as some market players had anticipated, the Central Bank said.

A spokesman said International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco would mull the fallout from Thursday's 25 basis point rise to 6.75 percent in the official British interest rate and decide next Monday when to issue the sterling bond.
"Next Monday he (Franco) will decide. This week it won't happen," the spokesman said.
He said Brazil's Central Bank had been given the "green light" from lawyers to issue the bond despite a reported court order in Italy to seize Brazilian assets.

An Italian court ruled on June 19 in favor of a group of companies who are suing the Brazilian government for failing to pay up after instructing them to buy coffee in a bungled bid to rig international prices in 1986.

The Central Bank said proceeds from a June 2 Italian lire Eurobond, which had reportedly been subject to the court order, had made it into the country without interference and lawyers had determined the sterling issue would not be affected.
"We've been given the green light by our lawyers. There is no possibility of the money being seized," the spokesman said.
